hookClip: India will always have a boss. Spain will always have lunch. Here's what to do — and what not to — in India and Spain.
countryADosClip: India. Address your manager as Sir, Ma'am, or Boss — well past your first year. Route requests up the chain and wait for sign-off, even on small matters.
countryADosScene: A modern open-plan office floor in Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex business district, glass towers visible through floor-to-ceiling windows behind her, Priya standing in the aisle between desks, weight shifted slightly to one hip, both arms hanging relaxed at her sides, face and eyes directly toward camera.
countryADosOutfit: A fitted deep teal sheath dress with three-quarter sleeves and a modest round neckline, tailored close to her curves to just below the knee, with a fine gold necklace and tan block-heel pumps.
countryADontsClip: India. Don't switch to first names with a skip-level manager uninvited. Don't email the CEO directly to save everyone time. Don't assume silence or ambiguous body language means agreement.
countryADontsScene: A glass-walled meeting room in a modern Mumbai office tower, a long conference table behind her and city buildings visible through the window, Priya standing facing the camera with her weight on her right leg, arms relaxed at her sides.
countryADontsOutfit: A fitted burgundy wrap blouse with three-quarter sleeves tucked into a high-waisted charcoal pencil skirt that hugs her hips, with tan pointed-toe pumps.
countryBDosClip: Spain. Use usted with senior colleagues until they invite tú. Build rapport over a long lunch before asking for a favour. Push back on an unreasonable deadline — it reads as competent, not insubordinate.
countryBDosScene: A sunlit rooftop terrace restaurant in central Madrid, classic cream-stone Madrid rooftops and domes softly out of focus in the background, no signs, billboards or readable text anywhere in frame, Priya standing at the edge of the terrace facing the camera with her weight on her left leg, both arms hanging relaxed at her sides, face and eyes directly toward camera.
countryBDosOutfit: An office-appropriate fitted terracotta midi sundress with wide shoulder straps, a modest square neckline and a cinched waist, skimming her curves to just below the knee, with a fine gold necklace and tan block-heel sandals.
countryBDosCaptions: Build rapport over a long lunch
countryBDontsClip: Spain. Don't assume first names from day one mean the hierarchy is gone. Don't expect a major decision to be settled by email alone. Don't schedule anything urgent for August and expect it to move.
countryBDontsScene: A bright co-working space in Barcelona's 22@ innovation district, floor-to-ceiling windows with the district's low skyline behind her, Priya standing facing the camera with a slight angle to her body, both arms hanging relaxed at her sides, face and eyes directly toward camera.
countryBDontsOutfit: An office-appropriate fitted sage-green midi sundress with wide shoulder straps, a modest V-neckline and a tie waist, fitted through the bust and hips to just below the knee, with small gold hoop earrings and nude block-heel mules.
